outputs.exact_statement: The polynomial [eq:polynomial] is homogeneous of degree $20$ and hyperbolic with respect to $e=(I_4,I_4,0)$, with $p(e)=1$. Its closed hyperbolicity cone $K=\Lambda_+(p,e)$ is not spectrahedral: for every finite $N\geq1$ and every real linear map $L:\mathbb S^4\times\mathbb S^4\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb S^N$, $$K\ne\{(X,Z,y):L(X,Z,y)\succeq0\}.$$

The quotient $q=p/\det X$ extends to a homogeneous polynomial of degree $16$ in the same $23$ variables. It is hyperbolic with respect to $e$, with $q(e)=1$, and $\Lambda_+(q,e)=K$. In particular, its closed hyperbolicity cone is not spectrahedral.

The form $b:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ defined in [eq:form] is nonnegative and nonzero. If a real bilinear form $\ell:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ satisfies $$\ell(z,y)^2\leq b(z,y) \qquad\text{for every }z,y\in\mathbb R^3,$$ then $\ell=0$.

The polynomial $p$ in [eq:polynomial] is homogeneous of degree $20$ on $\mathbb S^4\times\mathbb S^4\times\mathbb R^3$, a real vector space of dimension $23$. It satisfies $p(e)=1$ and is hyperbolic with respect to $e=(I_4,I_4,0)$.

Let $K=\Lambda_+(p,e)$. For real symmetric $X,Z$ and $y\in\mathbb R^3$, $$\begin{aligned}
 X\succ0:\qquad
 (X,Z,y)\in K
 &\ \Longleftrightarrow\ 
 Z\succeq\Phi_y(X^{-1}),
 \label{eq:slice-positive}\\
 (X,Z,0)\in K
 &\ \Longleftrightarrow\ 
 X\succeq0\ \text{and}\ Z\succeq0.
 \label{eq:slice-zero}
\end{aligned}$$ Moreover, $e$ lies in the interior of $K$ in the full ambient space.

Let $K=\Lambda_+(p,(I_4,I_4,0))$ for the polynomial in [eq:polynomial]. Suppose that $K$ admits a representation by a finite homogeneous real symmetric linear pencil. Then there are integers $a,c\geq1$, positive linear maps $$D:\mathbb S^4\longrightarrow\mathbb S^a, \qquad E:\mathbb S^4\longrightarrow\mathbb S^c, \qquad D(I_4)=I_a,\quad E(I_4)=I_c,$$ and a linear map $B:\mathbb R^3\longrightarrow\mathbb R^{a\times c}$ such that, for every $X\succ0$, $Z\in\mathbb S^4$ and $y\in\mathbb R^3$, $$\label{eq:schur-equivalence} Z\succeq\Phi_y(X^{-1}) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad E(Z)\succeq B(y)^\top D(X)^{-1}B(y).$$

Let $a,c\geq1$, let $D:\mathbb S^4\to\mathbb S^a$ and $E:\mathbb S^4\to\mathbb S^c$ be positive unital linear maps, and let $B:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^{a\times c}$ be linear. Assume that [eq:schur-equivalence] holds for every $X\succ0$, $Z\in\mathbb S^4$ and $y\in\mathbb R^3$, with $\Phi_y$ defined by [eq:phi]. Define $P(v)$ and $R(u)$ by [eq:projections]. For every pair of unit vectors $u=(u_0,u'),v=(v_0,v')\in\mathbb R^4$ and every $y\in\mathbb R^3$, $$b(v_0u'-u_0v',y) =\left\lVert P(v)B(y)R(u)\right\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^{2}. \label{eq:norm-identity}$$ Here the operator norm uses the Euclidean structures on the two block spaces.
